architectural_shift.hardcoded_logic_priority: Prompts and Templates are NOT database entries. They are hard-coded TS/Rust modules for maximum stability, performance, and minimal file bloat.

core_separation.TemplateBuilder: Constructs the structural 'frame' (e.g., Markdown layouts, JSON schemas).
core_separation.PromptBuilder: Assembles the 'message' by injecting data from the DB into hard-coded logic patterns.

1_Identity_&_Security.problem: Ensuring safe multi-user access with low infra overhead.
1_Identity_&_Security.tradeoff: 2FA is mandatory. We use Hard-coded Auth Roles (Admin/User) to avoid complex ACL tables.

2_State_Consistency.problem: Syncing Local SQLite with Cloud Postgres without data collision.
2_State_Consistency.tradeoff: Eventual consistency vs Blocking writes. We choose WAL-based async sync in Rust for speed.

3_Logic_Construction.problem: Managing Prompt/Template variety without database garbage.
3_Logic_Construction.tradeoff: Dynamic DB Templates (Flexible but messy) vs Hard-coded Logic (Rigid but clean/fast).
3_Logic_Construction.solution: We choose HARD-CODED. Logic lives in code, only 'Variable Values' live in DB.

4_Execution_&_Interactions.problem: Real-time AI responses vs Background long-running tasks.
4_Execution_&_Interactions.tradeoff: HTTP polling vs Streaming. We choose Vercel AI SDK (Streaming) + Rust MCP (Tools).

5_Observability_&_Recovery.problem: Silent failures in background workers or AI logic.
5_Observability_&_Recovery.solution: Diagnostic table with context snapshots for Rust-side analysis.
